data.text/markdown:
sverify: a guided tour

Somewhere downstream of every pipeline you write, someone is relying on it: the customer waiting for a refund, whoever gets paged at 3 a.m., the analyst whose dashboard has to add up. sverify checks the pipeline for them before it runs. You write the transformation in Ibis or SQL, as usual, and say what it may assume about its inputs and what it guarantees about its output. A checker written in Lean proves the guarantees for every possible input, or tells you why it can't. Then you get:
  1. Contracts proved, not tested. "No NULL city", "one row per device and minute", "no amount below zero" hold on every input that meets the preconditions, not just on yesterday's data: the checks you would write as dbt tests or expectations, done once, at definition time. Division by zero, integer overflow and bad casts are ruled out the same way.
  2. One plan, the same answer on every engine. The checked plan runs on DuckDB, Polars or DataFusion, or is written as Snowflake or Spark SQL, and means the same thing on each: NULLs, integer division, NaN, ties and overflow are spelled out, or the plan is refused where an engine can't match.
  3. Results kept up to date from the changes. Read the change feed of a Delta or Iceberg table, and update the result with plans proved to equal a full recompute, instead of a hand-written watermark job. Sinks write each state exactly once and carry the contract to the next job.

Start with a workflow

The first three chapters are complete jobs, condensed from the query catalogue of 139 real analytical queries. Each starts from source tables, states and proves a contract, runs on every engine, keeps up with new data and writes a sink, and each shows what goes wrong without the checker:
workflow sources and sinks what it catches
1 Duplicate card payments Delta, Change Data Feed a self-join matching rows with themselves; a watermark job missing a late duplicate and keeping a reversed one
2 Sensor alerts Iceberg LAG over ties; a NaN reading raising an alert; Snowflake and Spark tables without row order
3 An orders mart Delta, a type-2 dimension not_null(city) failing after a left join; / meaning three things on three engines

Thirty seconds of it

A transformation with a contract: the input has no negative amounts (requires), so the output has no negative and no NULL doubled (ensures). Calling the function asks Lean for a proof before the expression is handed back:

data.text/html:
postcondition status
(_.doubled >= 0) ✅ proved
_.doubled.notnull() ✅ proved
runtime ⚠️ may wrap around: ($2 * 2)
output column known values
id any integer or NULL
doubled an integer ≥ 22

data.text/markdown:
Both postconditions are ✅ proved, and the bottom table is what Lean worked out about every output column on its own: doubled is at least 22, because the filter keeps amounts of at least 11. Contracts explains how.

The rest of the tour

Features, one per chapter, with examples to change and break:
chapter what it covers
4 Contracts requires/ensures, what Lean tracks, on_unproved, contracts on real data
5 Keys and relations sv.unique, facts between columns, joins
6 Runtime errors division by zero, overflow, casts; proving they can't happen
7 Windows and ASOF joins LAG, LEAD, ROW_NUMBER, ties; aligning two sensors
8 Composing contracts proving one step's preconditions from the previous step
9 Incremental views a transform on a source becomes a node that refresh keeps up to date from changes alone; what is refused, and how the update rules work
10 Pipelines nodes over nodes, .write to store them, fallbacks, contracts that hold in every state
11 Engines and SQL DuckDB, Polars, DataFusion; SQL for DuckDB, Snowflake and Spark
12 Doubles, time and text NaN and −0.0, timestamps and intervals, calendar functions, strings
Under the hood, for when you want to know why the ✅ can be trusted:
chapter what it covers
13 Plans, meaning and proofs Substrait plans, Lean's interpreter, theorems, NULL
14 The checker substrait-check: well-formedness, Lean as a reference engine, Ibis coverage
15 What is proved, what is trusted the trusted boundary, a glossary and a map of the code
16 DataFusion's surprising semantics appendix: every DataFusion quirk, checked against the Lean model
17 One expression, many engines appendix: DataFusion, DuckDB, Polars, Snowflake and Ibis, question by question
No knowledge of formal verification is needed for any of it.

Opening the tour

Open the whole folder, so the links between chapters work: 
uvx marimo edit --sandbox notebooks      # from the project root
--sandbox gives each notebook its own environment with sverify installed from python/ (the first start takes a minute). The Lean checker must be built once with lake build (see the README's Development section). uvx marimo run --sandbox --include-code notebooks shows the same chapters as read-only apps.
